findings.text: POSIX queues order pending messages by a priority taken from the message type. Higher values are delivered before lower values, messages sharing a value keep arrival order, each distinct value has one group node in a balanced tree, insertion attaches to the existing group or creates one, and reception removes the oldest message of the highest group and discards the group when it becomes empty.

Queue accounting stays coherent across insertion, reception and teardown. A current count and a byte total grow and shrink together, the byte contribution equals the per message size, a cached pointer always designates the highest priority group, and at most one freed group node is retained for reuse while any surplus is released.

Reception tolerates tree and counter divergence by repairing rather than crashing. When no group exists yet the count claims messages, it warns once and resets the count. When the selected group is unexpectedly empty, it warns once, discards that group, and retries selection.

The observed queue state comprises protection and waiting primitives, two directional extended waiter lists, one shot notification registration with owner and namespaces plus cookie socket and execution identity, queued byte size and rlimit ownership, a priority tree with highest group hint and spare node, and an attribute block carrying maximum and current counts and maximum size.

Per queue state including tree, counters, waiter lists, notification fields and readiness checks is guarded by the per queue spin protection. Global queue count, rlimit charging, and namespace teardown handoff use a global message queue lock. Ucounts hash removal uses an irq saving hash lock, notification task lookup runs under read side RCU protection, and signal enqueue holds the target sighand lock. Callers keep the per queue lock enrolled across waiter enrolment and across drain collection during eviction.

Queue inode creation enforces namespace and privilege ceilings. Directory and regular modes diverge, defaults derive from namespace minima and explicit attributes override them, nonpositive limits are rejected, privileged callers face hard ceilings while others face namespace ceilings, size multiplications are checked for overflow, pinned accounting assumes one header per message plus one tree node per used priority capped by the priority range, and hierarchical rlimit charging must succeed or creation fails.

Eviction follows a drain then release lifecycle. After clearing, directories finish immediately. Regular queues collect every pending message into a temporary list under protection and release the spare node, then drop protection before releasing messages and rlimit charge, decrement the namespace queue count when a namespace is present, and drop ucounts and namespace references.

Filesystem bring up establishes no execution and no device semantics with page sized blocks and a queue magic plus queue super operations and uncached dentries. A sticky world accessible root directory is created. Mounts for a fresh namespace attach directly while other mounts use keyed lookup. Context setup pins current ipc and corresponding user namespaces, and namespace creation uses a longterm kernel mount that swaps in the target namespace.

Queue population is bounded per namespace. Creation checks the queue count against its maximum under the global lock with a privilege exemption, increments optimistically and rolls back on inode failure. Unlink shrinks directory size. Eviction decrements the count when a namespace is present. Namespace release nulls the superblock association under the global lock when enabled and otherwise is a no operation, then removes the namespace from its tree and defers final freeing through scheduled work.

Status, readiness and cleanup interfaces expose queue state without changing messages. Status read reports queued bytes and notification mode plus signal number and owner pid translated into the caller namespace and refreshes access and change times on success. Poll reports readable when nonempty and writable when below maximum after registering the wait queue. Flush cancels a notification only when the caller thread group owns it.

Synchronous waiting enrols the caller in a direction specific list ordered by scheduling priority, placing newcomers ahead of the first waiter whose priority value indicates equal or lower urgency. The sleeper drops queue protection during an absolute realtime bounded wait, then distinguishes woken readiness from interruption and expiry. Successful readiness returns without removal in the shown paths, while interruption and timeout remove the waiter under protection before returning.

Delivery completion performs at most one notification when the queue transitions from empty to one message, then always wakes ordinary waiters. Ignore mode does nothing, signal mode emits a message queue origin signal with mapped pid and uid after validating signal number and execution identity under RCU, thread mode stamps a wakeup marker into a cookie and forwards it through a socket. Registration is released exactly once after any attempt.

Pid helpers translate and manage identity safely across namespaces. Numeric lookup returns zero on missing pid or namespace, insufficient level, or namespace mismatch, and the active namespace derives from the caller task pid. Dropping the last pid reference invokes pidfs cleanup, cache release and namespace release, with final namespace release deferred to work. Task lookup from a pid returns the first thread group member or null and relies on RCU or tasklist protection as checked by a lockdep helper.

Privilege checks layer from broad to narrow. The outermost helper tests against the initial user namespace, the middle helper forwards with no options, and the common helper rejects invalid identifiers with a fatal diagnostic, consults the security hook with caller credentials, marks a superpriv flag on success, and reports a boolean outcome.

Resource charging propagates through nested user namespaces. Increment adds atomically at each level from the leaf upward, returning the leaf total unless any level goes negative or exceeds its ancestor ceiling, in which case it reports saturation. Decrement subtracts at each level, warns on negative totals, and reports whether the leaf reached zero. Dropping the last ucounts reference unhashes under irq safe protection, then releases the user namespace and frees through RCU.

Signal enqueue separates locking from policy. The outer helper acquires the target sighand protection and delegates, reporting missing target when locking fails. The inner helper preserves caller info except that it rewrites user ids across user namespaces and process ids across pid namespaces and forces kernel origin, explicitly privileged, and ancestor namespace deliveries.

Message destruction releases a possibly chained object. A security release hook runs first, the header is released, then each chained segment is released in turn with an opportunity to reschedule between segments.

Failures use ENOMEM for allocation and context and root cases, EACCES for missing namespace during creation, ENOSPC for queue count exhaustion without privilege, EINVAL for bad limits, EOVERFLOW for size arithmetic overflow, EMFILE for rlimit excess, ERESTARTSYS for signals during waits, ETIMEDOUT for wait expiry, and ESRCH for signal targets that cannot be locked.

New inode setup diverges by file kind. Regular queue inodes receive queue file operations, a fixed status size, fresh lock and wait structures, empty extended lists, cleared notification and accounting state, an empty priority tree with cleared hints and attribute defaults. Directory inodes receive directory operations, an extra link, and double entry size. All inodes get a fresh number, caller filesystem ownership, and timestamp initialization, with allocation and once initialization provided by dedicated helpers.

Insertion allocates its group node in atomic context and must propagate allocation failure without mutating counts or links. Eviction and segmented release never sleep while holding spin protection: pending messages are first collected under lock, then released after unlocking, with rescheduling allowed only during the unlocked segment walk.

Queue implementation refers to named constants MQUEUE_MAGIC for superblock identity, MQ_PRIO_MAX for priority range, HARD_MSGMAX and HARD_MSGSIZEMAX for privileged ceilings, FILENT_SIZE and DIRENT_SIZE for synthetic file sizing, EPOLLIN EPOLLRDNORM EPOLLOUT EPOLLWRNORM for readiness, and SIGEV_NONE SIGEV_SIGNAL SIGEV_THREAD plus SI_MESGQ for notification.
